epics.title: Core Experience and Identity
epics.jtbd: When a visitor lands on the site, I want to immediately understand the author's focus and have clear ways to contact them, so that I can explore their work or get in touch.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Zero visual regressions from Stitch mockups and 100% successful render of essays
requirements: R1: The site must implement the generated High-End Dark / Editorial design system without any debug terminal frames or telemetry logs on the frontend.
R2: The site must use grotesque headers and comfortable reading typography for essays and quotes.
R3: The site must include a clean, distraction-free reader view for essays and deontic logic articles.
R4: The site must include an aesthetic contact card.
R5: The implementation must be a pixel-perfect translation of the Stitch mockup into Svelte components.
R6: The reader must load and display published essays via an API, handling empty states and potential errors gracefully (completeness).
R7: Content authoring is handled externally; this epic is strictly bounded to the read-only presentation of published essays (completeness exception).
R8: The UI must be fully usable on mobile screens, provide visible interaction feedback, and meet WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards (keyboard operability, contrast, focus).

epics.title: Podcast Media Hub
epics.jtbd: When a visitor wants to listen to the podcast, I want to browse episodes with detailed show notes and audio playback, so that I can consume the audio content directly.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Zero audio playback initialization failures across major browsers
requirements: R1: The site must integrate a media hub for the 'Systems and Reality' podcast.
R2: The media hub must feature a functional audio player for episodes.
R3: The media hub must provide clear outbound links to external platforms like YouTube and Telegram.
R4: The podcast metadata and URLs must be fetched from an API and a defined database schema, providing fallback UI if the load fails (completeness).
R5: The UI must be fully responsive on mobile devices and accessible (WCAG 2.1 AA keyboard/screen reader compatible).

epics.title: Platform Telemetry and Measurement
epics.jtbd: When operating the site, I want to measure visitor engagement with my content and external links, so that I know if the site successfully drives interest in my work.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 100% of defined critical business events are tracked accurately
requirements: R1: The system must track reader engagement (essays viewed) to answer 'Are visitors actually reading the essays?'.
R2: The system must track podcast playback initialization to answer 'Are visitors listening to the podcast on-site?'.
R3: The system must track outbound clicks to YouTube and Telegram to answer 'Is the site successfully routing audience to external platforms?'.
R4: Telemetry must be implemented securely without exposing PII.

requirements: R1: The system must automatically perform regular database backups of all published essays and metadata.
R2: A full database restore must be actually performed and verified in a test environment to prove the backup strategy works.

epics.title: Privacy Consent Management
epics.jtbd: When a visitor arrives on the site, I want to be asked for consent before any non-essential trackers load, so that my privacy preferences are respected and the site complies with ePrivacy regulations.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 0 analytics trackers fired before explicit user opt-in
requirements: R1: The site must capture explicit opt-in consent before loading any telemetry or analytics scripts.
R2: The site must integrate an established consent management platform rather than building a custom banner.
R3: The user must be able to refuse consent with the same ease (same number of clicks) as accepting it.
R4: The user's choice must be recorded, and a persistent control must allow them to revoke or change their consent later.

slices.title: Integrate Consent Management Platform
slices.jtbd: When implementing privacy controls for this epic, I want to integrate a CMP, so that we can legally block or allow telemetry based on user choice.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a new visitor
When the site loads
Then the CMP banner must appear, offering equal options to accept or decline trackers
Given a returning visitor
When they wish to change preferences
Then a persistent link must reopen the CMP modal.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% of telemetry scripts successfully gated by CMP state

slices.title: QA Verification for Tracker Blocking
slices.jtbd: When implementing privacy controls for this epic, I want to verify that tracking scripts are strictly gated, so that we avoid regulatory breaches.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a visitor who has not consented
When they navigate the site
Then no analytics network requests must be initiated
Given a visitor who accepts and later revokes consent
When they revoke
Then subsequent tracking requests must immediately cease.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 0 network calls to telemetry endpoints without consent state=true
